thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT 3654321000 - Public S3 access detected for bucket `redwood-staging-logs`. Paging on-call @oncall.

emily: seeing a spike of `GET` requests to s3://redwood-staging-logs from odd IP ranges (ASN lookups: CN/UA). quick check via CloudTrail shows anonymous GETs since 03:12 UTC.

raj: oncall pinged. what's the immediate customer impact?

kevin: appears to be staging-only bucket. logs may contain debug headers and truncated auths. not seeing full prod tokens in initial samples, but need to confirm.

olivia: I'm going to sample objects with `--range` to avoid full downloads. command I'll run: `aws s3api get-object --bucket redwood-staging-logs --key app/2026-03-17/log1.gz --range bytes=0-2000 /tmp/sample.log` (won't paste contents here).

emily: 130 objects marked public-read since 03:12 UTC, last modified ~5m ago. source IPs: 185.14.72.0/24, 45.130.0.0/16, 93.91.0.0/16 (from CloudFront logs).

sec-bot: Automated scan: potential PII detected in sample (email addresses, internal hostnames). Severity flagged: medium.

oncall: taking incident. immediate mitigation plan: (1) lockdown bucket ACL/policy, (2) rotate staging service creds, (3) block offending IP ranges at edge, (4) scan for customer identifiers.

oncall: commands I'm about to run: `aws s3api put-bucket-acl --bucket redwood-staging-logs --acl private` then `aws s3api put-bucket-policy --bucket redwood-staging-logs --policy file://deny-public.json` — executing now. :lock:

kevin: also rotate `svc-staging-deployer` keys (long-lived) and invalidate any leaked temp creds. update CI secrets after rotation.

olivia: doing a targeted grep for `user_email` and `session_id` patterns. will redact and post summary to #sec-urgent (DMing legal first).

emily: initial grep shows mostly internal test emails, but I see 3 records with real-looking addresses (redacted). marking as potential customer impact pending deeper scan.

sec-bot: Audit summary: 7 distinct source IPs, ~200 GET requests, 1 PUT detected, timeframe ~03:12-03:20 UTC.

oncall: bucket ACL set to private ✅ (03:23 UTC). Applied deny-public policy ✅.

oncall: initiating svc-staging-deployer key rotation now. will invalidate old keys after new ones are in CI. ETA ~7m.

kevin: confirm replication/cross-account copies? if replicated, we need to lock targets too.

emily: replication disabled, no cross-account replication found. good.

olivia: extracting redacted samples for legal & privacy in DM. recommending forced password reset for any staging interactive accounts that may have exposed tokens.

oncall: svc-staging-deployer keys rotated and old access keys deactivated ✅. Jenkins staging deploys will need updated creds — pushing new key into secret store now.

oncall: deploy pipeline paused during key update, resuming once secret is updated.

emily: pipeline updated, smoke tests passing, staging deploys green.

raj: next steps: (A) full content scan for PII/customer identifiers, (B) prepare short incident notification for affected stakeholders, (C) legal/privacy review for breach threshold.

kevin: I'll open a ticket to rotate any long-lived staging creds we find and to review S3 bucket policies org-wide for similar misconfigs.

sec-bot: flagged objects count: 12 with potential identifiers. moving list to secure store.

olivia: sending redacted evidence to legal DM and creating `incident-3654321000` folder in secure drive.

oncall: updating incident tracker now. Preliminary assessment: likely low customer impact (staging-only, most are test accounts) but still treat as security event and run full assessment.

emily: CCing product & cs on the ops timeline in #incidents for FYI.

oncall: closing on-channel mitigation — bucket locked and keys rotated. will produce postmortem next week with root cause and checklist for preventing staging misconfig. thanks everyone. :heart:

kevin: filing follow-up task: add automated S3 public-access guardrail to infra PR checks.

raj: legal & privacy will advise on disclosure if needed.

incident-bot: Incident 3654321000 mitigated (status: mitigated). Postmortem assigned to @emily and @kevin.
